lines: Built with: vite.config.mjs, package.json declares @nextcloud/vite-config ^2.5.4 (locked 2.5.4), vite ^7.3.6 (locked 7.3.6).
Other delivered libraries: 25, axios 1.18.1, focus-trap 8.2.2, dompurify 3.4.13, @nextcloud/logger 3.0.3, @floating-ui/core 1.8.0, @floating-ui/dom 1.1.1, and 19 more.
Packages and versions are those the .license files beside the chunks name, since the source maps miss packages through the toolchain defect named here.

Known toolchain defect: vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js 4.0.1 in package-lock.json, where the CSS is injected by JavaScript, puts the code that injects the CSS in front of the chunk without shifting its source map, so the map the bundler combines from it loses sources. Here the map of cache/l10n-lint/recommendations/js/store-BcgVFaXw.chunk.mjs names 8 of the 22 packages its .license file names.
The app runs as built; only the map is short, so the frameworks and libraries are read from the .license files instead.

Built in a copy with @nextcloud/vite-config 3.0.0-beta.1, vite 8.3.5 (vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js 5.0.3), the build writes no chunk with both a map and a .license file, so nothing could be checked.

66 delivered files carry no source map, 3 files do. The bytes of the unmapped ones are charged only where the code shows its origin by itself: a copy of a file of the checkout, the glue of the bundler, code of the bundler and its plugins.
1 package is imported by their root in src, each delivered in fewer than 8 modules, so a per-module import has nothing to leave out and the specifier decides no bytes here.
